text:
Brayden Schenn is 35, a Stanley Cup winner in St. Louis, and now an Islander after 650 games as a Blue. He has 16 points in 23 games on Long Island, a fair start for a veteran in a new place, and 724 career points before this season.

The points are ahead of the play. His finishing is honest (six goals on 5.9 expected), but the Islanders have scored 5.9 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, and that kind of on-ice luck fades. The five-on-five picture is the concern: New York takes 46% of the expected goals with him on, seven points worse than without him. He still plays the game his way, 49 hits, and he exits the zone with possession 68% of the time in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season. Our range projects 41 to 60 points. His value now is as much in the room as on the scoresheet.
